newsitem.title: USA: Falcon CEO sees Q3 shr at or above estimates.
newsitem.headline: Falcon CEO sees Q3 shr at or above estimates.

text.p: Falcon Building Products Corp's orders are running at record levels, positioning it to meet or exceed third quarter Wall Street earnings estimates, the company's chief executive said.

"We're very comfortable with where the street's got us," Falcon Chief Executive William Hall said in an interview. Asked if that meant the company would meet or exceed current estimates, Hall replied, "I can't argue with that."
According to First Call, analysts estimate Falcon will earn $0.38 per share in the third quarter.
Hall said the company planned to grow sales to the home improvement market until they were about even with new home market sales.

"There's no question that housing is late cycle right now. We think there's enough pent-up demand that housing will be flat to modestly down," he said. "But the renovation and rehab market looks like it has another two to three years in it."
Falcon remains cautious about its 1997 outlook, Hall said, because the prospect of higher interest rates is a factor that weighs heavily over the housing industry.
However, Falcon's raw materials cost picture has improved considerably over 1995, when high prices hurt Falcon's results by about $0.25 per share, he said.
"We're feeling no pressure any place" on raw materials, Hall said.
